instruction.text: Which organisations train and provide lifeguards? Select the two correct answers.
Is this good advice for swimmers?

atoms.a: Don’t go swimming if you feel unwell.
Don’t go swimming on an empty stomach or straight after a large meal.
Get used to the temperature of the water slowly when entering.
Only jump into the water if you know it is safe to do so.
Arm bands, inflatable toys and lilos are not safe and do not protect you from drowning.
When swimming outside, get out of the water immediately if there is lightning, thunder, heavy rain or fog.
Be considerate of others at swimming pools; don’t run or push.
Shout for help and wave your arms if you are in trouble in the water. Help others when they have problems in the water. Never shout “help” as a joke.
Only go swimming if someone can help you if you have problems.
Let a responsible person know if you are going swimming.
Leave all of your rubbish on the beach.
Never swim if there is seaweed in the water.
Never swim for a long time.

atoms.b: Last week, I was at the swimming pool with my friends. We were playing catch at the edge of the pool. I accidentally bumped into a boy, who fell and hit his knee on the tiles.

instruction.text: Which advice did Leon not follow?

b: He did not tell anyone that he went swimming.
He went swimming when he felt unwell.

atoms.b: Yesterday evening, I went to the waterfront in our town alone. A thunderstorm was starting, which meant that the beach was completely deserted. When I was in the water, it started to rain heavily. The drops splashed on the surface of the water, and there was repeated thunder.

instruction.text: Which two pieces of advice did Carina not follow?

b: She jumped in where it was not allowed.
